01-tuned-intake-prepared-for-printing.jp.caption: The tuned runner in the slicer. Helmholtz resonance set the length needed to boost volumetric efficiency at the target RPM; printability set where it had to be split.

02-three-piece-printed-intake.JPG.caption: The intake printed in three sections with bolted flanges, so a runner longer than the build volume could still be produced and assembled.

03-dynamometer-assembly-and-instrumentat.caption: The dynamometer built to test it: the 212cc Predator engine on a plywood base, a torque arm and strap brake feeding a load cell, and Arduino instrumentation reading torque and RPM.

04-intake-cracked-at-the-flange.JPG.caption: The intake cracked at the flange while the dynamometer platform was being repositioned, before the comparison run against the stock intake could be completed. The instrument was validated; the part it was built to evaluate was not.
